newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Sellers hammer offers lower.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Sellers hammer offers lower.

text.p: Sellers continued to offer gas oil and jet fuel at lower levels on Tuesday and traders said the near term bottom is not yet in sight as buyers remained uninterested.

The softer tone was set earlier on the gas oil swaps market which followed through on Monday's plunge due to India's award of only four diesel cargoes for August delivery, exacerbating the soft regional demand.
July swaps lost another 50 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $20.90/$21.00, while August shaved off 40 cents to $21.60/$21.70

Physical offers followed suit, with four offers seen for July liftings. A European major offered 30,000 tonnes at $155 per tonne ($20.80 per barrel) for July 23-27 lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis, down from Monday's offer at $159 per tonne.
Another offer was seen at $20.90 for July 27-31 lifting fob.
"The market is at its lowest downturn at this point," one trader said. China has also not showed any interest to buy despite current low levels, he said.
But if prices remained low as the region enters the winter season, traders expect bargain hunters to emerge and curb a free fall in a contango market.
However, the glut in the MidEast continued to haunt the Asian market as well, traders said.
Demand has emerged from Nepal which has issued a tender to buy two 30,000-tonne cargoes of 0.5-percent sulphur diesel for August 11-20 and August 21-31 deliveries. The tender closes on July 15.
Jet fuel also fell with sellers continuing to offer lower to $22.90 for July 23-27 and $23.30 for July 25-29, compared with $23.60-$23.70 on Monday.
